questions.q: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
Which green pigment found in chloroplasts absorbs light energy during photosynthesis?
Which environmental factor is tested when a destarched leaf is partially covered with foil and exposed to light?
What gas is released as a waste product during photosynthesis?
Which part of a flowering plant is the primary organ adapted for carrying out photosynthesis?
What is the primary function of stomata on the underside of plant leaves?
a: To allow gas exchange (carbon dioxide in, oxygen out)

questions.q: Which layer inside a leaf contains the highest concentration of chloroplasts for maximum light absorption?
What chemical reagent is used to test a decolourised leaf for the presence of starch?
Why is a leaf boiled in ethanol during a starch test experiment?
a: To remove (decolourise) chlorophyll so color changes are clearly visible
To cook the leaf for consumption

questions.q: What role do guard cells play in a plant leaf?
a: To control the opening and closing of stomata
To manufacture glucose directly in darkness

questions.q: What is the balanced chemical formula for photosynthesis?
a: 6CO2 + 6H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6O2 (in presence of light and chlorophyll)

questions.q: What mineral ion do plants require to synthesize chlorophyll molecules?
What deficiency symptom appears in plant leaves when they lack sufficient magnesium ions?
a: Yellowing between veins (chlorosis) due to lack of chlorophyll

questions.q: Why do plants convert glucose into starch for storage rather than keeping it as glucose?
a: Starch is insoluble and osmotically inactive, preventing disruption of cell water potential
Glucose is toxic to plant cells

questions.q: What mineral ion is essential for plants to manufacture amino acids and proteins for growth?
What term describes a factor that is in shortest supply and restricts the rate of photosynthesis?
How does an increase in light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis up to a certain point?
a: It increases the rate of photosynthesis
It burns the leaf tissue instantly

questions.q: What happens to the rate of photosynthesis when carbon dioxide concentration in the air is increased?
a: It increases until another factor becomes limiting
It causes plant cells to burst

questions.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis eventually plateau at very high temperatures?
Which transparent waxy layer on top of a leaf reduces water loss by evaporation while allowing light to pass through?
What is the role of xylem vessels in plant leaves?
a: To supply water and mineral ions brought up from the roots

questions.q: What is the role of phloem tissue in flowering plants?
a: To transport sucrose and amino acids (translocation)

questions.q: In an experiment measuring aquatic plant photosynthesis (e.g., Cabomba or Elodea), what does counting the number of oxygen bubbles released per minute measure?
Why is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3) often added to water in aquatic plant photosynthesis experiments?
a: To provide a dissolved source of carbon dioxide

questions.q: What structural feature of spongy mesophyll cells aids gas exchange within the leaf?
a: Large air spaces between cells allowing carbon dioxide to circulate freely
A tight arrangement with no gaps

questions.q: How are leaves broadly adapted to absorb maximum light energy?
a: They are broad and flat, providing a large surface area

questions.q: What happens to stomata in most plants during darkness?
Which light wavelengths are most effectively absorbed by chlorophyll for photosynthesis?
What is the primary purpose of glucose produced during photosynthesis in plants?
a: To be used in respiration for energy, or converted into starch, cellulose, or proteins
To act as a waste product excreted through roots

questions.q: Why is chlorophyll green in appearance?
a: It reflects green light while absorbing red and blue wavelengths

questions.q: What experimental control is required when testing if carbon dioxide is necessary for photosynthesis?
a: Placing the plant in total darkness for a week
Using soda lime to absorb carbon dioxide from the surrounding air in a sealed bell jar

questions.q: What is the compensation point in plants?
a: The point where respiration stops completely
The time of day when plants stop growing
The light intensity at which the rate of photosynthesis exactly equals the rate of respiration
